issues.title: Overbroad applicability claim for disconnected linear Lie groups

failure_location.quote: The construction is generic for any linear Lie group and relies on building a matrix constructed from the Lie algebra whose kernel is spanned by a group-equivariant and permutation-invariant basis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Whereas $O(3)$ is not a connected group, our approach can still be applied to its two connected components separately.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the Lie-algebra construction is generic for every linear Lie group, including disconnected groups. The old paper actually develops the general construction for a connected linear Lie group and treats O(3)'s two components separately. The distinction is material: for the disconnected linear group {±1}, all Lie-algebra derivatives vanish, so infinitesimal constraints cannot distinguish a trivial representation from the sign representation even though the element −1 imposes an additional global equivariance condition. Thus the supported generic scope is connected linear Lie groups, not arbitrary linear Lie groups.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract and repeated conclusion overstate the generic applicability of the construction; the connected-group formal results and the separate O(3) extension remain unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise every generic applicability claim in the abstract and conclusion to state that the Lie-algebra kernel construction applies to connected linear Lie groups. Clarify that disconnected groups require additional constraints for their nonidentity components, while retaining the separately established O(3) treatment.
issues.why_classification: The formal setup assumes connectedness, and examples such as {±1} show that the Lie algebra alone cannot detect component-group equivariance. Thus the advertised scope must be substantively narrowed, precluding typo or minor classification. Nevertheless, the connected-group claim remains recognizably comparable and all formal results are preserved through a local prose correction, so neither global reconstruction nor major mathematical loss is required.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: In this article, we have introduced a direct numerical method for efficiently constructing group-equivariant (GE) and permutation-invariant (PI) spaces, valid for arbitrary linear connected Lie groups.

issues.title: GE-PI kernel coefficients indexed by the wrong set
issues.failure_explanation: The rows and columns of M^{l,L} are declared to be indexed by the class set overline(M)_l×M_L. A vector in its kernel therefore supplies one coefficient per class, not one coefficient for every element of the larger raw set M_l. The theorem's sums and coefficient-family declaration over M_l are consequently undefined or dimensionally incompatible. Its proof starts with a sum over the class set and establishes the class-indexed version found in v2.
issues.overall_effect: The literal GE-PI basis formula, and the analogous following corollary, are not well-defined even though the intended class-indexed result is proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Theorem thm:GEPI_basis and the analogous following corollary, index every coupling-coefficient family and basis-function sum by the class set overline(M)_l rather than the raw set M_l, while retaining the output index set M_L.
issues.why_classification: The declared dimensions of the matrix, the preceding class construction, and the proof uniquely force class indexing. The proof already establishes exactly that version, so the repair is a transcriptional set-index correction requiring no change to any inference or guarantee.

issues.title: Reversed kernel inclusion in the GE half-matrix proof
issues.failure_explanation: If M2x=0, then every selected row also vanishes and therefore Mupx=0. Thus deleting rows gives ker(M2)⊆ker(Mup). The old proof asserts the opposite inclusion solely because Mup consists of rows of M2, so that inference is invalid. Together with the equal nullities already obtained in the proof, the correct inclusion yields the claimed equality.
issues.overall_effect: The equality of kernels in the GE half-matrix proposition is not concluded by the written argument, leaving the reduced basis and ensuing dimension formulas unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted inclusion by ker(M2) ⊆ ker(Mup), since Mup consists of selected rows of M2. Combine this correct inclusion with the equal nullities already established in the proof to conclude ker(Mup) = ker(M2); all listed downstream basis and dimension results then proceed unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The written row-deletion inference is genuinely invalid and therefore is not merely typographical. Its correction is nevertheless an elementary, one-line linear-algebra argument using facts already proved, with no new lemma, weakening, or change to the affected guarantees.

issues.title: Wrong lowering multiplicity in the specialized GE-PI matrix
issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:M_GE_PI assigns an off-diagonal transition m'=m_(j,p,q) the factor λ_{m'^(j),q}. In the lowering branch of eq:M2-PI, q=p−1, so the required factor is λ_{m'^(j),p−1}. The old p+1 factor can count a different value and hence define a different matrix. The old later block eq:MLpL-PI already uses p−1, exposing the inconsistency internally.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed specialized matrix is inconsistent with both the general GE-PI matrix and the class-indexed blocks used in its kernel proof; a literal implementation could compute a different kernel.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the lowering branch of eq:M2-PI, replace the multiplicity λ_{m'^(j),p+1} by λ_{m'^(j),p−1}. Keep the resulting formula consistent with eq:M_GE_PI and the later block eq:MLpL-PI.
issues.why_classification: For the transition q=p−1, the general matrix formula uniquely forces the p−1 multiplicity, and the subsequent block calculation already uses it. Thus this is a uniquely recoverable index transcription with no repair to the proof architecture or mathematical guarantees.

issues.title: Reversed kernel inclusion in the GE-PI half-matrix proof
issues.failure_explanation: Because Mup contains only a subset of the rows of M2, every vector in ker(M2) lies in ker(Mup); removing rows can only enlarge the kernel. The old proof instead claims ker(Mup)⊆ker(M2) from that row relation. Once the direction is reversed, the already derived equality of nullities yields the claimed equality of kernels.
issues.overall_effect: The written proof does not establish the GE-PI half-matrix kernel equality, and therefore does not support the reduced basis and dimension chain until the inclusion is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted inclusion by ker(M2) ⊆ ker(Mup), because deleting rows can only enlarge the kernel. Use the equality of nullities already obtained in the proof to deduce ker(Mup) = ker(M2), leaving the reduced GE-PI basis and dimension chain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes an invalid kernel-inclusion inference, so the defect is substantive rather than a typo. The correct inclusion and the existing nullity calculation give a short, routine, complete repair with no new argument of substance and no loss of any affected result.

issues.title: Missing weight in the GE-PI full-rank calculation
issues.failure_explanation: Substituting K=−L−1 into the weighted ladder identity eq:ladder-pi gives a positive term 2(L+1)W_{−L−1}, not 2(L+1)I. The factorial weight W is generally not the identity. Consequently eq:fullrank-pi is false as written, although replacing I by the forced positive-definite weight recovers the intended full-rank conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof's first full-rank justification does not follow from its cited weighted ladder identity, so the GE-PI half-matrix proposition and its dimension consequences are unsupported until this calculation is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct eq:fullrank-pi by retaining the weight forced by eq:ladder-pi: the final positive term after setting K=−L−1 is 2(L+1)W_{−L−1}, not 2(L+1)I. Since W_{−L−1} is already defined to be positive definite, the intended full-rank conclusion and its dependent results remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Direct substitution into the displayed weighted ladder identity uniquely forces the omitted factor W_{−L−1}. The proof uses only positivity, which the source already establishes for W, and never needs W to equal the identity. Restoring the missing factor therefore requires no new inference or loss of guarantee.

issues.title: False zero-derivative constancy corollary
issues.failure_explanation: The preceding theorem concerns a representation, but the corollary's scalar function ρ is merely a linear combination of representation entries and need not itself be a representation. For the connected linear group G={diag(e^t,e^{-t}):t∈R} with its defining representation, ρ(g)=tr(g)=e^t+e^{-t} is such a linear combination. Its derivative at the identity is zero, but it is nonconstant. Hence the corollary is false and cannot justify the converse implications from the infinitesimal kernel equations to global equivariance.
issues.overall_effect: The necessity of the kernel conditions remains valid, but their claimed sufficiency for global GE and GE-PI functions—and the basis, recursion, specialized dimension, asymptotic, and O(3) results relying on that sufficiency—was not established by the old argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace cor:constant_zero with the connected-group integration-of-intertwiners lemma: if finite-dimensional continuous representations π and σ and a linear map C satisfy dσ(X)C = C dπ(X) for every Lie-algebra element X, then σ(g)C = Cπ(g) for every g in the connected group. Prove this by passing to exponentials through the power series and then using that every group element is a finite product of exponentials. In the GE proof, identify M c=0 with this derived intertwining relation; in the GE-PI proof, apply the same lemma to the induced representation on the class-indexed PI space, verifying that representation from its stable class basis. This restores the exact basis theorems and hence every listed recursion, dimension, asymptotic, and O(3) consequence.
issues.why_classification: The scalar constancy corollary is false and cannot support the converse implications by a symbolic edit. Recovering them requires a genuinely different, nontrivial representation-theoretic lemma and a contained reformulation of both sufficiency proofs, especially for the induced GE-PI representation. The argument is nevertheless local to those proofs, uses the existing connectedness assumptions, and preserves all affected statements without global reconstruction or mathematical weakening.
